# Next Greater Element I. An entry of -1 means that number has no next
# greater element.

@example After 7 comes 8, after 2 comes 9 at once, and nothing after 9 is greater than 9.
[7,2,9]
[2,9,5,7,8]
=> [8,9,-1]

@example After 3, the numbers 1 and 2 are skipped and 5 is the first greater one. Nothing after 6 is greater.
[3,6]
[6,3,1,2,5,4]
=> [5,-1]

@example 8 is the first number after 5 that is greater; 50 is greater too, but it comes later.
[5]
[5,1,8,50]
=> [8]

# The smallest input.
[0]
[0]
=> [-1]

# nums2 increasing: each answer is the number right after it.
[40,10,50]
[10,20,30,40,50]
=> [50,20,-1]

# nums2 decreasing: no number has an answer.
[6,9,3]
[9,8,6,3,0]
=> [-1,-1,-1]

# The bounds 0 and 10^4. The largest number never has an answer, wherever
# it sits.
[10000,0]
[0,10000,7]
=> [-1,10000]

# Greater numbers before the last one don't count.
[3]
[20,15,3]
=> [-1]

# Smaller numbers are skipped, the nearer of two greater numbers wins, and
# two numbers share an answer.
[8,3]
[8,1,3,2,9,12]
=> [9,9]

# nums1 holds all of nums2, in another order.
[5,2,6,0,4]
[4,0,6,2,5]
=> [-1,5,-1,6,6]

# Values that don't fit in a byte: 300 and 44, 256 and 0, 1000 and 232
# share their lowest 8 bits.
[44,300,256]
[300,44,256,1000]
=> [256,1000,1000]

# waits for 1000, which comes at the very end.
